knowledgeAnswers.rationale: An injury is a safety event, so the injury and incident record with immediate action comes first. A performance appraisal, a warning or an overtime request does not record the event.

A rating is defensible when each area has an observable standard defined in advance and evidence is recorded against it. General impression, length of service and popularity are not evidence of performance.

Documented feedback and support come first, then an improvement plan with a review date if the result does not change. Immediate suspension, removal without a record and waiting for the annual review skip the steps.

practicalCriteria: An incident record for a practice scenario has facts, people, immediate action and a follow-up date.
An appraisal sheet defines each area by an observable standard, with an evidence column for each rating.
An improvement plan template has a support action, a named contact and a review date.
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80 per cent pass mark (all 3 of 3 correct for this lesson). A quiz pass is not verified practical competence. The incident record, appraisal and improvement plan are assessed separately by an assessor against the practical criteria.
evidenceRequired: Practice incident record, appraisal sheet and improvement plan template reviewed by an assessor
stopWorkCriteria: Stop any disciplinary step where an injury or safety event has not first been recorded and handled under the safety procedure.
Stop any suspension or dismissal until qualified advice has been obtained.
